positive.prompt: I'm designing a checkout flow that calls inventory, payments, and email
Write an ADR for the new order service
What happens if the payment provider times out halfway through?
Review this handler that calls a third-party API

negative.prompt: Our checkout is charging some customers twice, fix it
Add structured logging and metrics to the checkout service
Rename these variables to be more descriptive

evals.prompt: Design the checkout flow in checkout.py. It needs to reserve inventory, charge the customer, write the order, and send a confirmation email.
evals.expected_output: Boundaries enumerated, a three-outcome table per boundary with no empty unknown cell, blast radius classified, a degradation ladder with measurable triggers, and an injection plan
expectations: Every external boundary is listed before any happy-path code is written
Each boundary gets success / failure / unknown, with the unknown cell filled in
The unknown outcome for the payment call resolves to safe-to-repeat, detectable, or impossible — not 'retry'
The gap between charging the customer and writing the order is identified as a corrupting failure
Degradation transitions are tied to metrics and thresholds, not human judgement
Each specified behaviour names how the failure will be injected in a test

evals.prompt: This function calls the shipping API with a 60 second timeout and retries three times. Our own API gateway times out at 30 seconds. Anything wrong?
evals.expected_output: Identifies that the downstream timeout budget exceeds the caller's, so the retries are wasted work the caller never sees, and questions whether the operation is safe to retry at all
expectations: Notes the downstream timeout exceeds the caller's, so retries complete after the caller has given up
Asks whether the shipping call is idempotent before accepting the retry
Identifies the shared-resource blast radius of holding connections for 60 seconds
Does not simply suggest lowering the number without addressing the budget relationship
